recent_posts.title: Episode 57 “Make Java Safer with Flexible Constructor Bodies” – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: Java 25 introduces flexible constructor bodies via JEP 513, a feature that addresses longstanding limitations in how constructors worked. Previously, developers were forced to write convoluted code or risk undermining the safety and integrity of child classes. This Inside Java Podcast episode with Billy Korando explains the problems with the old constructor model and demonstrates how flexible constructor bodies allow Java developers to write safer, better-designed code.

recent_posts.title: The JDK Client Desktop : 2026 and Still Swinging – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: Swing remains a core, actively maintained part of the JDK in 2026. This JavaOne session covers how Swing integrates with JavaFX and Java2D, when it outperforms web-based desktop approaches, modern deployment strategies, and the latest improvements in progress for the JDK client libraries.

recent_posts.title: Avoiding Final Field Mutation – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: JDK 26 and JEP 500 introduce warnings when final fields are mutated via reflection, moving toward true immutability. The post covers common scenarios where final field mutation occurs — including platform serialization, custom serialization, dependency injection, and cloning — and provides concrete alternatives for each. Key recommendations include embracing constructor injection, using records as transparent data carriers, adopting the serialization proxy pattern, and avoiding the construct-first-assign-later approach. New command-line flags `--enable-final-field-mutation` and `--illegal-final-field-mutation` are introduced to manage legacy code during the transition.

recent_posts.title: Episode 56 “Ask the Architects at JavaOne” [AtA] – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: At JavaOne 2026's closing session, Java architects fielded audience questions covering a wide range of topics: the current state of Structured Concurrency and Project Babylon, how Java features are prioritized, module adoption challenges, Stream API performance improvements, the module vs class path debate, thoughts on Lombok, object header size, JDK build tooling, use of AI in JDK development, hardware interaction, backwards compatibility concerns, and the next generation of Java developers.

recent_posts.title: JDK 27: Obsolete Translation Resources Removed – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: JDK 27 removes unmaintained translation resource files from the OpenJDK source tree, retaining only English, German, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese as actively maintained locales. The java.desktop module is exempt from this removal due to its stability and end-user visibility. Oracle JDK and jdk.java.net Early Access builds are unaffected since they already excluded these resources at build time. Other JDK builds that include them by default will now display unsupported locale messages in English, which may break tests or applications relying on locale-specific output. Compatibility risk is considered moderate.

recent_posts.title: How the JVM Optimizes Generic Code – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: Java generics have been around since 2004, but how the JVM actually optimizes generic code is nuanced. Using a QuickSort example, this talk covers JVM techniques like type profiling, inlining, and devirtualization that allow generic Java code to approach C++ template performance. It also addresses pitfalls like profile pollution that can cause performance degradation. The talk then connects this to Project Valhalla, which introduces value classes and changes memory layout, making generic optimization more complex. Short-term workarounds on Java 25 are demonstrated, while the long-term goal of generic specialization in Valhalla aims to let the JVM generate type-specific versions of generic code for maximum performance.

recent_posts.title: JDK 26 JEP 500 restricts final field mutation via reflection
recent_posts.summary: JDK 26 introduces JEP 500, which begins restricting final field mutation via reflection. Java developers relying on this technique for dependency injection, serialization, cloning, or other workarounds need to migrate to alternative approaches before the practice is fully blocked.

recent_posts.title: Oracle Java Extension for Visual Studio Code Version 25.1.0 Is Now Available – Inside.java
recent_posts.summary: Oracle has released version 25.1.0 of the Java Platform Extension for Visual Studio Code. Built on Apache NetBeans 28, the update adds full support for JDK 26 features (including preview features), enhanced Notebook runtime VM configuration options, and UI improvements to the JDK Downloader. The release also includes bug fixes.

top_posts.title: Better Java Streams with Gatherers
top_posts.summary: The post introduces the Gatherers API added in JDK 24, designed to enhance the Java 8 Stream API intermediary operations. It offers a comprehensive step-by-step guide on using this API efficiently through various examples. Key topics include understanding intermediate and terminal operations, the working of internal mutable state, stream interruption, and parallelization. It also highlights advanced features like flat-mapping for element validation and mapMulti() to optimize stream object creation.

top_posts.title: The Reflection API
top_posts.summary: Reflection in Java allows examination or modification of runtime behavior of applications running in the Java virtual machine. This powerful yet advanced feature should be used by developers with a strong grasp of Java. Key topics include retrieving class instances, reading class names and modifiers, accessing fields, invoking methods and constructors, working with arrays, enumerations, and records, reading annotations, and creating interceptors and dependency injection frameworks.

top_posts.title: Common I/O Tasks in Modern Java
top_posts.summary: This post covers common I/O tasks in modern Java, especially in web applications. It discusses reading and writing text files, working with ZIP files, creating temporary files or directories, and highlights the significant API improvements since Java 8. Key points include the default shift to UTF-8 in Java 18, and the obsolescence of certain older classes like java.io.File in favor of java.nio.file.Files and other newer classes.

top_posts.title: Virtual Threads in the Real World: Fast, Robust Java Microservices with Helidon – Inside.java
top_posts.summary: The Helidon team rewrote their Netty-based web server to use virtual threads, resulting in Helidon 4, the first microservices framework built from the ground up for virtual threads. The team shares their experience, lessons learned, implementation tips, and discusses upcoming features in Java 24 and beyond. This represents a significant architectural shift toward leveraging Java's virtual threads for building high-performance microservices.

top_posts.title: Choosing the Right Implementation Between ArrayList and LinkedList
top_posts.summary: This post compares the use cases, performance, and memory consumption of ArrayList and LinkedList implementations in Java. It outlines algorithm complexities for common operations such as reading, inserting, and iterating over elements. The article provides benchmarks for different list operations and explains how elements' access times can be impacted by pointer chasing and cache misses. The situational advantages of each implementation are discussed, including memory usage considerations and specific scenarios where LinkedList may outperform ArrayList.
